descripcion:
Oracle CEO pay: $627.4 million in fiscal 2026 for one of its two CEOs, against $94,740 for the median employee.
From the archive: Sep 2026. Not today's news.

What is a CEO pay ratio? Public companies must report it in their proxy statement (the document sent to shareholders before the annual meeting): the CEO's total pay compared with the pay of the median employee, the one in the exact middle of the payroll. Oracle's proxy, dated Sep 25, 2026, says: "our success is driven by the quality of our people." Then it lists the pay. The math: $627,472,419 ÷ $94,740 = about 6,623. That is 6,623 median salaries in one year of one CEO's pay (Clayton Magouyrk).

Read it right: Oracle has two CEOs. This is one of them. The proxy gives the other, Mr. Sicilia, $256,606,752. Magouyrk's total is mostly one equity-award column ($621,669,237, the grant-date value of a stock award, not cash) against a salary of $942,308. The median is the median global employee, per the proxy. A ratio, not a cause.

The quality of our people. Here is the median. (Our take.)

Sources:
- SEC EDGAR · Oracle, Sep 25, 2026: «At Oracle, our success is driven by the quality of our people, who we believe are among the best and brightest in the industry.» and «The fiscal 2026 total compensation of Mr. Magouyrk was $627,472,419, the fiscal 2026 total compensation of Mr. Sicilia was $256,606,752 and the fiscal 2026 total compensation of our median global employee was $94,740.» https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341439/000119312526402816/orcl-20260925.htm
